_comment: Bearer token -> the approving principal that token IS. Read by BOTH sides of the WordPress live-core harnesses: reeflex-core is started with REEFLEX_RESOLVER_TOKENS pointed at this file (core accepts a path as well as inline JSON), and wp-stubs.php's reeflex_harness_token_for() looks up the token to send for whichever principal a scenario approves as. One file so the two sides cannot drift; adding a principal to a harness means adding one line here. Synthetic fixture credentials for a throwaway local core -- never deploy this file.
_comment_actor: conformance-demo.php's H10 proves the four-eyes guard (check 5) refuses a resolve where the approver IS the raising agent. Since 0.2.0 check 4 runs first, so without a credential bound to that identity H10 would be refused principal_not_verified and would never reach the guard it exists to test -- a 403 for the wrong reason, scored as a pass. This binding exists so H10 keeps testing what it claims to.
